facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Chapter 1 runs one night at Cutler Row, from the fourth division to the sixth; it is the same night the Ferriby tin was opened.
facts.quote: The same night, from the fourth division to the sixth.

facts.subject: Qiu Yinzhi
facts.fact: Yinzhi wrote her full four-part name (surname, generation character, given name, courtesy name) at the docket head in the lineage-hall hand; Wystan checked and blotted it; the name is never rendered on the page.
facts.quote: Surname, generation character, given name, courtesy name.

facts.subject: Qiu Yinzhi
facts.fact: Yinzhi is entered on the Register docket as assay of record, over Wystan's signature as Warden of Duty for the Night Register.
facts.quote: He wrote *assay of record* under her name, and under that his own, *W. Ashmore, Warden of Duty, for the Night Register*, and the division.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: His hands tremor; the brass strike needed his elbow on the bench and his left hand pressed over his right.
facts.quote: He set his elbow on the bench and laid his left hand over the back of his right and pressed, and the tremor went down into the bench instead of into the seal.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: He has lived with the smell of brass wax for eleven years.
facts.quote: Resin came up off it, and under the resin a metal smell he had lived with for eleven years and still could not have named.

facts.subject: Brass wax
facts.fact: Brass wax is a dull yellow stick the Division issues only to its officers.
facts.quote: The Register's wax came out of the forms drawer: brass wax, a dull yellow stick the Division issued to its officers and to nobody else.

facts.subject: Ferriby wedge
facts.fact: The wedge's crown shows a quarter inch of new growth inside the sealed chapter tin, logged in the day-book margin as 'crown +¼ in sealed, 11d'.
facts.quote: The number was already in ink in the margin, *crown +¼ in sealed, 11d*, and the same eye an hour later would only give him the same number with less sleep behind it.

facts.subject: Ferriby wedge
facts.fact: The growth continued inside a Fixatio tin whose seal was whole; Wystan recorded that in the day book.
facts.quote: Something in the tin had gone on running under a seal that was sold to the courts as a promise that nothing would.

facts.subject: Ferriby wedge
facts.fact: Chain of custody: Tally cut the wedge in the North Ferriby cut; Yinzhi sealed it there under chapter wax on the 9th; the chapter's tin was found whole; its seal was broken at Cutler Row by the assay in the officer's presence.
facts.quote: Cut in the cut by Tally, N., and sealed there by the assay under chapter wax, the 9th.

facts.subject: Ferriby wedge
facts.fact: The wedge was moved by gloved forceps into a fresh Division Fixatio tin, sealed with brass wax and struck with Wystan's brass: Register file Ferriby, exhibit one.
facts.quote: Contents moved by forceps, gloved, to a Division tin; brass wax; struck.

facts.subject: Chapter's tin
facts.fact: The chapter's emptied tin was left unwashed, upright at the far end of the scullery sill.
facts.quote: He stood it upright at the far end of the sill, away from the wash-tray, where nobody could put it in the vinegar by mistake.

facts.subject: Ferriby tin
facts.fact: Wystan holds that the exhibit is no longer the Society's; the chapter may ask the Division in writing and will be refused.
facts.quote: From this division it is not the Society's.

facts.subject: Chapter wax
facts.fact: Four pieces of the broken chapter seal (two from the front-room blotter, two from under the desk) fit the join; folded in a druggist's paper, labelled and dated, laid on the sill beside the tin.
facts.quote: He wrote on the outside, *Chapter wax, Timberline. Broken by the assay at Cutler Row in the officer's presence. Four pieces.*

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: A taste of green from the wedge stays at the back of his tongue through three rinses and grounding tea; he does not record it. Unresolved.
facts.quote: He had nothing to put against that. He did not write it down.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Appearance: tall and narrow, hair tied at the nape and hanging to the waist, dark red in lamplight, a white line through the left eyebrow.
facts.quote: The black glass gave him back a tall, narrow man with his hair tied at the nape and hanging to the waist, dark red where the lamp caught it, and a white line through the left eyebrow.

facts.subject: Qiu Yinzhi
facts.fact: LIE: Yinzhi tells Wystan her bracelet stopped pulling at the sink. It did not (her thumb is on the badly struck mark as she says it). Uncorrected; Wystan believes it.
facts.quote: It went quiet when you were at the sink.

facts.subject: Tally
facts.fact: Tally's insert was dated the 14th and is held open at the Night Register.
facts.quote: Your insert of the 14th has been read at the Night Register and is open here.

facts.subject: Tally
facts.fact: Wystan's letter asks Tally to rewalk the line as before the 11th, measure the same way and log each find at the time in a notebook kept on his person: a second dataset from the same observer.
facts.quote: I want a second dataset from the same observer.

facts.subject: Tally
facts.fact: The letter asks who set the parish marker on the Ferriby line and when, and what the animals drank or licked from.
facts.quote: Tell me what the animals on that line put their mouths to: water, licks, troughs, anything that is set out and filled.

facts.subject: Letter to Tally
facts.fact: The letter is signed 'Night Register, Cutler Row' under brass wax and goes with the Society's bag in the morning bundle; the nine-word wire was rejected.
facts.quote: He signed it *Night Register, Cutler Row*, dropped a thumb of brass wax beside it, and set the brass in the wax.

facts.subject: Night Register
facts.fact: The Night Register has been one officer for four years, in a scullery on Cutler Row whose main goes off at the eleventh division; a Prime Warden's minute could fold it.
facts.quote: It had been true for four years, since the Division wanted a particular officer somewhere else and found him a scullery on Cutler Row with a main that went off at the eleventh division.

facts.subject: Qiu Yinzhi
facts.fact: Yinzhi was eight months capped and burned two coils.
facts.quote: If it comes to a hearing, and it will not come soon, somebody will stand up and say the assay was eight months capped and burned two coils and cannot say what she read.

facts.subject: Qiu Yinzhi
facts.fact: Wystan sends Yinzhi home; she may tell the chapter the tin is under his brass at Cutler Row and they may write.
facts.quote: Tell them it is under my brass at Cutler Row and they may write.

facts.subject: Qiu Yinzhi
facts.fact: Yinzhi knows Wystan counts forty-two minutes, and tells him to eat something at the sixth.
facts.quote: "Then you counted."

facts.subject: Ferriby site
facts.fact: Eleven hinds and a stag died inside a quarter mile, the last twenty-two paces short of the parish boundary marker; clean ground beyond, checked twice by Tally.
facts.quote: The last of them twenty-two paces short of the parish boundary marker.

facts.subject: Ferriby site
facts.fact: Four ravens in the birch would not come down to the carcasses.
facts.quote: Four ravens in the birch that would not come down.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: His Register position, written in the day book under 'edges': a dose goes where it is put. (Held as true by him; see the misreading.)
facts.quote: A dose goes where it is put.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: MISREADING: Wystan concludes the formulator's dose stops where it was put, so every site will show a hard edge. True of Ferriby's first site only; false of every dose after.
facts.quote: Whatever the formulator had put into those animals had stopped where he stopped putting it, because a man who works at a distance from his own work has to choose the distance, and every site in the four counties would show the same hard margin once somebody walked it with a rule.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: The Ferriby hind is the forty-second minute in the back of his day book.
facts.quote: At the back of the book, on the pages he kept for them, he entered the forty-second minute beneath the other forty-one.

facts.subject: Cutler Row
facts.fact: The main came back on at the sixth division; Wystan logged 'main on, 6th'.
facts.quote: The main came back at the sixth division.

facts.subject: Day desk
facts.fact: The Division's day desk is at the front of the same Cutler Row building, up four steps from the passage.
facts.quote: He lifted it the way he lifted everything, two fingers and a thumb at the rim of the lid and the base, and he took the docket form in the other hand, and he went out through the front room and along the passage, where the hum ran under the boards the whole length of the house, and up the four steps to the front of the building where the Division kept its day desk.

facts.subject: Brack
facts.fact: The docket book's Ferriby entry carries Brack's Bureau return: Wellspring bleed, Verdantia, tertiary expression, no operator indicated, no file; ruled off in red and marked closed.
facts.quote: Two lines had been ruled under it in red.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Wystan's memorandum opens Register file Ferriby under the red rule, does not dispute the measurement, and puts 'edges' in the margin by Brack's line; the docket form is folded in at the page.
facts.quote: In the margin, level with Brack's line, he wrote one word.

facts.subject: Day clerk
facts.fact: An unnamed day clerk (about fifty, bald crown with grey fringe, wen by the nose, brown coat buttoned wrong, black sateen oversleeves) reads only Brack's line, calls it closed and shelves the book unread.
facts.quote: He shut the book over the memorandum, over the folded docket and the one word in the margin, took it off the lectern in both arms and slid it into its place on the shelf behind the counter, spine out.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: At the end of the night the Ferriby tin sits on the scullery sill beside the chapter-wax fold, with his brass lying on the lid.
facts.quote: Wystan picked up the tin by its rim, two fingers and a thumb, and carried it back down the passage over the hum to the sill, and set it beside the fold of chapter wax, and laid his brass on the lid.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Chapter runs Day 1 from noon to the ninth division.
facts.quote: He woke at noon with the shutters closed and the house humming under him.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: His hands shake with a fine fast tremor at waking, worse in the right; the Division filed it as a disciplinary observation.
facts.quote: The Division had entered it in his file under a different heading, in the copying hand, as a disciplinary observation.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Holding himself suppressed asleep leaves his jaw and shoulders aching each morning.
facts.quote: He had kept himself down all night, asleep, the way he kept himself down awake, and this was what it came to in the mornings.

facts.subject: Keld's minute
facts.fact: Keld's minute is held by Wystan and checked each morning against a written record; the minute first, then the paper.
facts.quote: The minute came first and the paper after, because a record read first is a record remembered, and after that the minute would only agree with it.

facts.subject: Keld's minute
facts.fact: The written record's exact text, in brown ink gone tea-coloured, folded in four in Wystan's coat.
facts.quote: *Keld, O. Door on the landing. Handle iron, cold. Right hand. Lamp behind. Count at thirty-one. Legs tired. Not afraid. Bread, dark, butter. Says: "Sixth. They said the sixth. Hold it to the sixth."*

facts.subject: Keld's minute
facts.fact: On Day 1 the minute matched the record exactly, forward and backward.
facts.quote: It had not moved.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Wystan was the second man through the landing door and took the minute off the handle; the relief came late.
facts.quote: The first had his arms full, so it was Wystan who put his hand on the handle, and that was how he had the minute.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: His brass token was left on the tin lid at Cutler Row at the sixth division; he went to the medical house without it.
facts.quote: His brass was lying on a tin lid on Cutler Row, where he had left it at the sixth division, and he gave his name at the porter's hatch with nothing in his hand.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: He retrieved the brass from the tin lid and put it in his waistcoat.
facts.quote: He put it in his waistcoat.

facts.subject: Brass token
facts.fact: The Register's token is brass because the Night Register is not a full desk; carried four years, never asked to change it.
facts.quote: He had carried it four years and had never asked to have it changed.

facts.subject: Keld
facts.fact: Keld's Division coat hangs on a peg in his room with his silver token still in it.
facts.quote: Nobody had ever come to take it back.

facts.subject: Keld
facts.fact: Keld lives in the upper-floor end room of the Division medical house, two streets over behind the stables.
facts.quote: Keld's room was on the upper floor at the end.

facts.subject: Keld
facts.fact: Keld counts under his breath to varying numbers (twelve, nineteen, seven, four, thirty); Wystan cannot find what he counts.
facts.quote: He could find nothing in the street that Keld was counting.

facts.subject: Keld
facts.fact: Keld asks for 'them' and repeats 'They said the sixth'; the orderly says he asks twice, same as always.
facts.quote: "Twice. Same as always."

facts.subject: Keld
facts.fact: Keld taught Wystan the druggist's fold in the back room of the old office on the river.
facts.quote: Keld had taught him to fold a paper the druggist's way.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Six people alive know what Stage Wystan holds; Keld knew first but is not counted among the six.
facts.quote: Keld was alive.

facts.subject: Elspeth Lyle
facts.fact: Prime Warden Elspeth Lyle is one of the six who know his Stage; she had it off his file the week he was put on nights.
facts.quote: She had had it off his file the week he was put on nights, and she had read it, and had said nothing then, and had said nothing since.

facts.subject: Elspeth Lyle
facts.fact: Prime Warden Elspeth Lyle, about sixty, the only person in the building who calls him 'Warden of Duty'.
facts.quote: She was the only person in the building who used the title, and she used it as other people use a surname in a quarrel.

facts.subject: Night Register file
facts.fact: The Register may keep the file open until the quarterly inspection of the gauge-housing and not a day longer; entered in Lyle's minute in ink under her silver seal, initialled by Wystan.
facts.quote: *The Register may keep this curiosity open until the quarterly inspection of the gauge-housing, and not a day longer. E. Lyle, Prime Warden.*

facts.subject: Night Register file
facts.fact: The Register's position, copied into Lyle's minute: a dose goes where it is put, and every site will show the same margin.
facts.quote: The Register's position is that a dose goes where it is put, and that every site will show the same margin when somebody walks it with a rule.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Wystan initialled both position and term; his hand shook on the second initial.
facts.quote: His hand shook on the second initial and he did not stop to steady it.

facts.subject: Elspeth Lyle
facts.fact: Lyle signs the northern office's quarterly return together with the gauge-housing seal on inspection day.
facts.quote: At the inspection the Board's man reads my housing and seals it, and the northern office's return goes up the same day under the same seal, and I sign the two together.

facts.subject: Elspeth Lyle
facts.fact: Lyle refuses to put the Night Register on the return quarrelling with the Bureau.
facts.quote: "I will not put the Night Register on that return quarrelling with the Bureau over deer."

facts.subject: Day clerk
facts.fact: The day clerk heard 'eleven hinds and a stag' and wrote something in his ledger.
facts.quote: She said it back to him quite flatly, and the clerk at the end of the counter wrote something very small in his ledger.

facts.subject: Edwyn Brack
facts.fact: Edwyn Brack, Bureau, about fifty, coil-burn scar on right thumb; had seen the memorandum.
facts.quote: "I have seen your memorandum."

facts.subject: Edwyn Brack
facts.fact: Brack stands by his classification: bleed, Verdantia, tertiary, no operator.
facts.quote: It's bleed. My man took it off a calibrated coil against the standard and it's bleed, Verdantia, tertiary, and there's no operator in it.

facts.subject: Bureau field sheets
facts.fact: Brack gave Wystan the Bureau's raw Ferriby field sheets with coil calibration, in a green-taped folder, unasked.
facts.quote: "No. Master Brack gave them to me in the passage."

facts.subject: Bureau field sheets
facts.fact: Lyle orders the sheets entered as received unasked, today, before he reads them.
facts.quote: "Then enter them as received unasked, today, with the division, before you read a line of them."

facts.subject: Elspeth Lyle
facts.fact: LIE: Lyle says she did not send for Brack (she did; tell: the pen did not stop, eyes on the green tape). Uncorrected.
facts.quote: "I did not send for Master Brack."

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: MISREADING: Wystan believes the residue settling in a shut room falls on everyone alike; in fact it runs to him (H13).
facts.quote: It was what any shut room did by this hour, with the main running under it and people at work in it all day, and it came down on everybody in the room alike; Lyle had simply never sat a night on the Register, and had nothing on her hands to feel it with.

facts.subject: Edwyn Brack
facts.fact: Brack heard Wystan say he will get a hand and not a purse.
facts.quote: "I will get a hand and not a purse."

facts.subject: Greyshaft Nine
facts.fact: Chapter 2 runs one night at the Greyshaft Nine coldhouse, the second division to the ninth; it is the twelfth day Vesk has watched Malphas (eleven days, the twelfth begun at the second division).
facts.quote: The twelfth had started at the second division and he had never asked.

facts.subject: Greyshaft Nine
facts.fact: The main under Greyshaft Nine has been capped four years; the standpipe housings on the west wall are dead, there is no meter and no bill; the row was struck off the Board's schedule.
facts.quote: The main under Greyshaft Nine had been capped four years, and the standpipe housings along the west wall stood there in their brackets with nothing in them, iron gone the colour of an old kettle, capped and unbilled and quietly rusting into the slate.

facts.subject: Greyshaft Nine
facts.fact: The drip in the coldhouse's far corner runs twenty-two drops a minute; Vesk counted it a year ago and still counts it.
facts.quote: Twenty-two drops a minute.

facts.subject: Greyshaft Nine
facts.fact: The housing gauge reads four degrees in the coldhouse.
facts.quote: What there was instead was the one thing Vesk could not get past: the Lord had been sitting on an iron bench in a room the housing gauge had at four degrees since the first division, with no gloves on and his coat folded beside him and not under him, and his fingers were the colour of a living man's fingers.

facts.subject: the ninth hind
facts.fact: The ninth hind, eleven days under the ferment, is structurally liquid and cellularly whole; Nuvalik moves her off the rail onto the slate table at the second division.
facts.quote: Eleven days of the ferment had taken the connective net out of her and left the meat where it was.

facts.subject: the ninth hind
facts.fact: Nine carcasses hang on the rail, eleven days, no smell; the crown growth stands nine inches at best.
facts.quote: Eleven days on the rail and no smell and nine carcasses signed by nobody, and it had been beautiful work and it had been an argument about what a thing is.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: Vesk built the contractile matrix into the third-dilution formulation on one pour (in since the eleventh hour, stood just under an hour).
facts.quote: Into it, at the dilution, so that the thing that grew and the thing that pulled came off the same pour and arrived in the same tissue at the same time.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: Vesk has gone four days without sleep.
facts.quote: That was the whole of the last four days and he had not slept through any of them.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: Vesk's hands close only two thirds of the way; he carries anything in both flat palms.
facts.quote: He looked at his hands on the bench and made them close, and they got two thirds of the way and stopped.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: Two grafts on Vesk's hand: the first clean, the second holds but grips badly; its two fingers grow ridged yellow nails he cuts every fourth day and hides from the lamp.
facts.quote: The second had taken in the way that a thing takes when it has been asked twice, which was well enough for holding and badly for gripping, and the nails on the two fingers that took had come in ridged and yellow and had never stopped growing since.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: Vesk's home village laid flat beck stones on graves, one a year for nine years, until the ground was finished.
facts.quote: Flat ones, out of the beck, one a year for nine years, until the nine were on and the ground was finished.

facts.subject: Ilmar Foss
facts.fact: Malphas calls Foss by his given name, Ilmar.
facts.quote: "Ilmar," Malphas said.

facts.subject: Ilmar Foss
facts.fact: Foss has the gauge-housing open, its seal broken on a quarterly inspection that stopped coming nine years ago.
facts.quote: He had the coil out again, in pieces, the jeweller's glass screwed into his eye, and the brass of the gauge-housing open beside him with the slate back off it and the seal broken on a quarterly inspection that had stopped coming nine years ago.

facts.subject: Malphas
facts.fact: Malphas wants the Arbitration Division's Warden-of-Duty field manual for its unsigned attribution paragraph; he has designed against it for two years from hearsay.
facts.quote: The manual has a section on attribution and the section has a paragraph in it that nobody signed, and every officer who works a residue works it off that paragraph, and I have never read the paragraph, and I have been designing against it for two years out of what other people tell me is in it.

facts.subject: Arbitration Division field manual
facts.fact: The field manual is a numbered issue logged against a name in an issue book and surrendered when an officer is struck off, dies or goes to the Bench.
facts.quote: It is a numbered issue.

facts.subject: Ilmar Foss
facts.fact: Foss held a numbered instrument for eleven years; when struck they took the instrument before the oath.
facts.quote: I had a numbered instrument off the same kind of book for eleven years and the day they struck me they wanted the instrument before they wanted the oath back.

facts.subject: Ilmar Foss
facts.fact: Foss refuses to wire for the manual: a wire is nine words and the flimsy is kept at both ends for a turn of fourteen days.
facts.quote: A wire is nine words.

facts.subject: Ilmar Foss
facts.fact: Foss will ask men in turn for a copy of the manual; it will take a season, and Malphas accepts a season.
facts.quote: It will be a season.

facts.subject: Nuvalik
facts.fact: Malphas told Vesk the fourth hind's shoulder gave contraction twice; Vesk has had nothing like it from the others.
facts.quote: The Lord said contraction.

facts.subject: Nuvalik
facts.fact: LIE: Nuvalik tells Vesk everything the fourth hind gave her is written down. It is not: she got contraction twice and did not record it (tell: blade wiped on the apron first). Uncorrected (H08).
facts.quote: Everything the fourth hind gave me is written down.

facts.subject: Nuvalik
facts.fact: Nuvalik's tell: she wipes the blade on her apron before she speaks; it frightens Vesk.
facts.quote: She wiped the blade on her apron before she spoke, which was the one thing about her that frightened him, and it did not frighten him less for happening every day.

facts.subject: the book
facts.fact: The cell's book is kept on the shelf over the ice press, kept by Nuvalik since the first night; nobody else has taken it down.
facts.quote: It is on the shelf over the press where it has been since the first night and nobody has taken it down but me.

facts.subject: Nuvalik
facts.fact: Nuvalik's name was worn by three people before her; she says she has spent all three of hers in this room.
facts.quote: The name I wear was worn by three people before me.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: The pour: four places along the near flank, not the wound, a count of forty between each; the colour cleared inland, faster at the two forward pours.
facts.quote: He worked it in at four places along the near flank, a little at each, and between each he stopped and gave it the count of forty and watched the colour go out of the surface as the channels took it away inland.

facts.subject: Ilmar Foss
facts.fact: Foss, at the glass, calls the synthesis filthy and correct and wants both findings in the book.
facts.quote: It is filthy, and it is correct, and those are two separate findings and I want both in the book.

facts.subject: Malphas
facts.fact: Malphas's hands keep a living man's colour after sitting ungloved on an iron bench at four degrees since the first division (H07).
facts.quote: What there was instead was the one thing Vesk could not get past: the Lord had been sitting on an iron bench in a room the housing gauge had at four degrees since the first division, with no gloves on and his coat folded beside him and not under him, and his fingers were the colour of a living man's fingers.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: MISREADING: Vesk believes the ice press's warm air along the east wall explains why Malphas's hands never take the cold (worked out the fourth night, never said). Never corrected; never paid as recognition.
facts.quote: The press threw its warm air along the east wall and the gauge bench stood in the middle of it, and that was the whole of why the Lord's hands never took the cold.

facts.subject: the ninth hind
facts.fact: Nuvalik states the hind: no Crystal, no self, a net that shortens toward the emptier end.
facts.quote: She is meat with a new net in it and the net can shorten.

facts.subject: the ninth hind
facts.fact: No anchor in the hind and there will not be one (an anchor is a binding, a binding takes a name); she cannot be told where to go, only given somewhere emptier.
facts.quote: Four to six without an anchor, and there is no anchor in her, and there will not be one.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: Vesk claims she needs only eleven feet since the building is the emptiest place in four streets; Malphas answers she has not yet got up.
facts.quote: Then she will not need four days.

facts.subject: Malphas
facts.fact: Malphas orders the night written up in the book, in ink, with the division, under the project's name, by four hands.
facts.quote: I want the whole of this project written down under the name I gave it, by four hands, in one book, because the file somebody builds out of us will be built off what is written and I would rather it be built off this than off a clerk's recollection of it.

facts.subject: the ninth hind
facts.fact: The hind does not stand. The hide at her shoulder draws up once, a hand's breadth, untouched; Vesk tells nobody and does not call Foss's glass to it.
facts.quote: He did not call Foss back to put the glass on it.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: Vesk ends the night writing the division in the book's margin.
facts.quote: Then he went to the shelf for the book and wrote the division in the margin.

hooks.text: Tally found clean ground on the far side of the parish marker, twenty-two paces past the last carcass, and checked it twice; Wystan writes 'ask Tally who set the marker'. Paid when the lick-keeper's round is found to end at the marker: the carrier turned home there.

events.what: Wystan's letter asks Tally who set the parish marker and what the animals on the line drank from; Tally's clean far side, checked twice.
events.quote: Tell me who set the parish marker on the Ferriby line, and when, if anybody knows.

hooks.text: A quarter inch of new growth inside a Fixatio-anchored tin with the seal unbroken; the day book reads 'crown +¼ in sealed, 11d'. Paid at the hearing: Fixatio held what it was given, and what it was given was a running working.

events.what: A quarter inch of new growth under an unbroken Fixatio seal, logged 'crown +¼ in sealed, 11d'.
events.quote: Something in the tin had gone on running under a seal that was sold to the courts as a promise that nothing would.

hooks.text: 'They are chapter wax and I will want them later.' Four pieces of the broken seal, dated and kept. Paid at the hearing: the pieces fit the join and prove custody.

events.what: Four pieces of chapter wax fit the join, folded and dated for custody.
events.quote: The day somebody wants to say this tin was opened on the road, I want four pieces of chapter wax that fit a join, and a paper round them dated before anybody asked.

hooks.text: Wystan asks Tally to keep walking and measuring: 'I want a second dataset from the same observer.' Paid when the notebook is taken from Tally's walking body, complete to the night he died.

events.what: Wystan asks Tally for a notebook kept on his person: a second dataset from the same observer.
events.quote: I want a second dataset from the same observer.

hooks.text: The bulletin clerk told Tally the Night Register was a person. The cell knows its hunter only as the Night Register. Paid when the Register is folded and Malphas closes the line.

events.what: The bulletin clerk told Tally the Night Register was a person; one line in a minute could fold the desk.
events.quote: A desk could be folded into another desk by one line in a Prime Warden's minute.

hooks.text: Wystan holds everything by the very edge, two-fingered, even a cup. Paid in VI: Salter sees a man holding a cup that way across the quad, notes it, and nothing follows.

events.what: Wystan holds his tea by the rim, thumb and two fingers, away from his palm.
events.quote: He gave her one and took the other to the window, and he held it there by the rim, the thumb on one side and two fingers on the other, so that none of the heat came near his palm.

hooks.text: Malphas's hands keep a living man's colour in a four-degree coldhouse. Paid in the hearing gallery, at the verdict, as a detail Wystan notices and never explains; never recognition.

events.what: Malphas's fingers keep a living man's colour after sitting ungloved at four degrees; Vesk explains it away by the press.
events.quote: What there was instead was the one thing Vesk could not get past: the Lord had been sitting on an iron bench in a room the housing gauge had at four degrees since the first division, with no gloves on and his coat folded beside him and not under him, and his fingers were the colour of a living man's fingers.

hooks.text: Nuvalik got contraction out of the fourth hind's shoulder twice and did not report it; Malphas 'will discuss with her separately'. Paid when the discussion happens.

events.what: Vesk asks about the fourth hind's twice-reported contraction; Nuvalik says it is all written down.
events.quote: Everything the fourth hind gave me is written down.

hooks.text: Nuvalik carries a name three people carried before her and thinks she has spent all three on this work. Paid when she sets down the name she wears in the cell and leaves; she does not inform.

events.what: Nuvalik tells Vesk her name was worn by three before her and she has spent all three in this room.
events.quote: The name I wear was worn by three people before me.

hooks.text: Vesk's grafted fingers, the ridged yellow nails that will not stop growing; the village that put stones on its graves. Paid when he dies of his own formulation and Nuvalik lays stones on his walking body.

events.what: Vesk's two grafts and ridged yellow nails; his village's nine grave stones.
events.quote: The second had taken in the way that a thing takes when it has been asked twice, which was well enough for holding and badly for gripping, and the nails on the two fingers that took had come in ridged and yellow and had never stopped growing since.

hooks.text: 'Where I was raised, the sky finishes what the ground starts, and when the sky refuses, people walk out to see why.' Paid when the ravens will not come down to Tally and he walks.

events.what: Nuvalik gives the saying about the sky finishing what the ground starts.
events.quote: Where I was raised, the sky finishes what the ground starts, and when the sky refuses, people walk out to see why.

hooks.text: Keld's minute, taken off a door handle, lucid, waiting for relief; checked every morning against a written record. It slips by a word after Cutler Row; paid when it is set right at Keld's bedside.

events.what: Keld's minute checked against the written record; it has not moved; relief came late.
events.quote: It had not moved.

hooks.text: Wystan's Shell rests near zero saturation; free residue in a closed volume runs toward him. The dead lean to the quiet. He believes they are being sent to him; paid when he learns he is the sink and nobody sent them.

events.what: Residue settles on Wystan in Lyle's shut room; he misreads it as falling on everyone.
events.quote: It began on the backs of his hands first, as it always did, where the stain was.

hooks.text: The Register token is brass, not silver, because the Night Register is not a full desk, and he has never asked to have it changed. Paid when he hands it in.

events.what: Brass token explained against silver; carried four years, never asked to change it.
events.quote: The Register's token was brass because the Night Register was not a full desk.

hooks.text: Suppression held waking and sleeping; six people alive know what Stage he is. Paid when he drops it in the death-house and the whole cordon knows.

events.what: Six people alive know his Stage; Lyle is one of them.
events.quote: *Six people alive know what Stage I hold.*

hooks.text: Deming: thirty-one days of usefulness left, and Malphas has already counted them. Paid on the thirty-first day.
'In eleven weeks somebody in a room in the capital will look at the Swale line and see a bad spring.' Paid when the Logistics return publishes.
'I would prefer the file be built off a word I chose.' Every letter names Project Zombification. Paid when the Bench titles the file by the word and every thread ends in it.
'That is how they found the Hollow Shaft people. They found a name in a private correspondence.' Paid when the precedent is read into the record at Deming's hearing.

Foss reads the Division field manual's unsigned paragraph on anamnetic reading and its counters; Malphas adopts them as house rules. Paid when a moved wall makes Wystan's Called Late at Greyshaft Nine confidently wrong.
'The ninth hind is the freshest and she is the one I want.' Paid when she stands up off the table and leans to the standpipe.

events.what: The ninth hind on the table with the matrix pour in her; she does not stand, the hide draws up once.
events.quote: The ninth hind is the freshest and she is the one I want.

hooks.text: Foss pays the carter in salt bars because salt bars leave no bill; the salt bar is money that can be eaten. Paid when the parish dead walk out of the pit with the bars in their purses.
Wystan's margin note: edges. Paid when the walkers erase them and he strikes the word in public.

events.what: Wystan writes 'edges' in the docket-book margin level with Brack's line.
events.quote: In the margin, level with Brack's line, he wrote one word.

events.what: Lyle reads 'edges' in the margin; the position goes into her minute.
events.quote: She read *edges* and the plain sentences underneath it, and then *A dose goes where it is put*, and took up her pen, and copied the line into the minute in a small upright hand, and wrote the date and the division beside it.

hooks.text: Brack's classification: Wellspring bleed, Verdantia, no operator indicated, correct off a true measurement. Paid when the Accord's official classification stays bleed and Brack signs it again.

events.what: Brack's Bureau return in the docket book: bleed, no operator, no file; closed.
events.quote: A day clerk had entered it in the copying hand, the Bureau's return pinned to the leaf beside it, signed in its own ink: *Wellspring bleed, Verdantia, tertiary expression, no operator indicated. No further action. No file. E. Brack, Lattice Classification Bureau, northern office.*

events.what: Brack stands by bleed and says he would sign it again.
events.quote: I'd sign it again this afternoon.

hooks.text: STAY's counter: threaten something outside the boundary; two Enforcement men have used it. Harrow is one. Paid when Wystan drops STAY to save the family on the stair.
Article XX: a death-house may not be cut; the exemption is claimed far more often than granted. Paid when Wystan holds the Wicket death-house under STAY and the dead are entered on the roll.
Deming decides that whatever the Accord asks he will not give it the hand. Paid when the Ruling chair asks and he refuses under reservation.
Malphas promises Foss release with his own name when the work is done. Paid when Foss takes a bench under his own name and informs no one.
When the Bench reserves the hand, the exhibits return to the filing party: the Ferriby tin and the chapter wax go back to Timberline. Paid when the tin is the lesson at Aetherion.

The Society tells Wystan the academies ask for field instruction; at Aetherion, Mu-jin has promised Class X the Night's Watch for 'field work, real cases'. Paid when Wystan takes the class to a real case.
At the Aetherion the hum stops at one door, the west range; Wystan stands there and turns back east. Paid when he does it again at the end of the week and goes no further.
His technique gets the hand, never the purse; Article XV prosecutes only the purse. This case inverts it. Paid when he teaches it: the hand or the purse, never both.

events.what: Wystan tells Brack he will get a hand and not a purse; Brack answers that Fifteen wants the purse.
events.quote: "I will get a hand and not a purse."

summaries.title: The Docket Head
summaries.summary: Wystan checks and blots Yinzhi's full name at the docket head and enters her as assay of record. Gloved, he moves the Ferriby wedge with forceps into a fresh Division Fixatio tin, seals it with brass wax and strikes his brass into the seal. He logs it in the day book as Register file Ferriby, exhibit one, "crown +¼ in sealed." He collects the four pieces of chapter wax. He folds them in a druggist's paper, dated, for custody. Over grounding tea he asks whether the bracelet is still pulling, and Yinzhi says no. He rejects a nine-word wire and writes Tally a letter: walk the line and measure into a notebook, a second dataset from the same observer, who set the marker, and what the animals put their mouths to. He signs it "Night Register, Cutler Row." He enters the Register's position, "A dose goes where it is put," and records the forty-second minute. The main returns at the sixth division. At the day desk he writes his memorandum under Brack's closed classification, with *edges* in the margin. A day clerk reads only the classification and shelves the book.

summaries.title: Twenty-Two Drops
summaries.summary: Day one, the second division to the ninth, at Greyshaft Nine. Nuvalik brings the ninth hind down off the rail onto the slate table. Vesk has built the contractile matrix into the third-dilution formulation on one pour and lets it stand, then carries the flask in both palms and works it in at four places along the near flank, the count of forty between each. The colour clears inland, faster at the two forward pours; Foss, at the glass, gives the reason (the trunk quit last, the forward channel is finest, the finest channel pulls hardest) and calls the synthesis filthy and correct, wanting both findings in the book. Malphas asks Foss to get the Arbitration Division's field manual for its unsigned attribution paragraph; Foss refuses a wire and says it will take a season, and Malphas accepts a season. Nuvalik states what the hind is: no Crystal, no self, a net that shortens toward the emptier end. Malphas orders the night written up in ink under the project's name by four hands. The hind does not stand. Vesk sees the hide at her shoulder draw up once, tells nobody, and counts the drip to twenty-two.

summaries.title: The Morning Check
summaries.summary: Day 1, noon to the ninth division. Wystan wakes with his hands shaking. He recalls Keld's minute, then reads the written record against it word for word. It has not moved. At the medical house the porter admits him by his face, because his brass is on the tin lid at Cutler Row. Keld sits at the window counting under his breath at something Wystan cannot find. He asks "Is that them" and says "They said the sixth." At the day desk Prime Warden Elspeth Lyle reads the edges memorandum and calls the file a curiosity. The Register may keep it open until the quarterly inspection of the gauge-housing and not a day longer. In the upper passage Brack stands by bleed and hands over the Bureau's raw Ferriby field sheets unasked. In Lyle's shut room the position and the term go into her minute in ink, under her silver, and he initials both. Residue settles on his skin and he does not remark it. Lyle orders the sheets entered as received unasked and denies sending for Brack. At the ninth division Wystan tells Brack: "I will get a hand and not a purse."
